## TL;DR

Round 3 closes the two review findings and the edge cases from round 2. The task-debugger and repo-guide chat panels now get disc and decimal list markers, because both were missing from the shared rule in `style.css`. The supervised "waiting" line now carries `release-update-status`, so it sits on its own row instead of sharing one with Cancel. The marker guard test no longer relies on a hand-kept list of six surfaces. It scans every direct `v-html` markdown render site, so a new surface without a rule fails the test. The headless update-banner harness passes 135 of 135 checks on a rebuilt UI.

## Work and rationale

The review's bug was a class of defect, not two files. Preflight sets every list to `list-style: none`, so any container that renders markdown and does not restore markers loses its bullets while keeping its indent. My first step was to enumerate every direct `v-html` markdown site in `src/ui-app/src`, not just the two the reviewer named. That found six: `playground-markdown`, `cto-markdown`, `debugger-markdown`, `pm-markdown`, `td-markdown` and `guide-markdown`. The `md-rendered` and release-notes containers bind through variables, so they are not direct call sites. Both are already in the rule.

I added `.td-markdown` and `.guide-markdown` to the shared `list-style` rule for `ul` and `ol`. The reviewer also suggested having `renderChatMarkdown()` emit a marker class. I did not do that. The renderers return an HTML string, and the containers belong to the components. Adding a wrapper element would change the DOM, which the chat layout depends on. Instead the guard test in `src/ui-app/tests/markdown-list-markers.test.ts` now walks every `.vue` file, finds each `v-html="renderMarkdown(` or `renderChatMarkdown(` element, and requires that one of its classes has both marker rules. The test also checks that each site has a class and that the scan finds at least six sites. A new chat panel now fails the test until its class is added to the rule.

The supervised waiting line in `ReleaseUpdateNotification.vue` had only `release-update-muted`. Its CSS comment and round-2 report claimed the own-row layout, but the class that creates that layout was missing. I added `release-update-status`. The test in `releases.test.ts` now expects exactly two occurrences of that class, one for the supervised line and one for the hand-run line.

The QA doc had drifted in two places. It quoted a test name that did not exist, and it described the old six-surface table. I corrected both, and I removed a review-history sentence I had added, since QA docs should not carry review history.

## Approaches tried

My first grep for the call sites failed because the unquoted `--include=*.vue` glob did not expand in zsh. Re-running it with quoted patterns worked. My first version of the scan test expected at least eight sites. Only six are direct calls, so I corrected the threshold to six and kept the sanity check, since a silent zero would make the rule test vacuous. I also first wrote a skip for `engineering-report-body`, a modifier class on a shared container. That was the wrong shape. The test now asks whether any class on the site has the rule, which is what the CSS actually needs.

## Challenges and blockers

Running vitest directly from the repo root failed to transform `.vue` files. It works with `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts`, which is what `test:vitest` uses. The scoped `repoos check` passed, but its tests step was skipped because this runner sets `REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1` and RepoOS runs the suite on the remote validation runner. I cleared that variable and ran the full suite myself. My first foreground attempt hit my own 550-second timeout at roughly 350 of 794 tests. In that partial run three unrelated suites showed failures, `release-status`, `debugger-integration` and `mtd-docs-fast-path`, two of them at the 30-second timeout. All three passed in isolation (73 of 73), so I attribute them to load on the parallel run, not to this change. The full suite was rerun in the background, and the result is recorded in the activity note.

The restart itself is still unproven on a real server. The harness faked the restart POST and recorded that honestly in the QA doc. A human should run one real hand-run restart on a disposable server if that proof is needed. This is not something I could verify here, and I did not claim it.

## Key learnings

A guard test that keeps a hand-written list in sync with the source will drift. The reviewer found that exact failure in round 2. Scanning the source for the pattern the guard protects is cheap and closes the gap. The scan does not cover variable-bound `v-html`. Those sites rely on the `md-rendered` class, which is in the rule and in the test list. The playground indent test still pins the exact formatting of `ModelPlaygroundPanel.vue`, so a reformat could false-fail it. I left that alone because it is minor and a change would not add coverage.
